It does not merely describe the phenomenon of "culture wars"; it adopts a highly critical and normative tone, labeling the issue as "manufactured outrage" and a "deliberate strategy" to distract. Rather than explaining the sociological drivers of polarization (e.g., media echo chambers, algorithmic reinforcement, or genuine value shifts), it immediately aligns with a specific partisan grievance: that political actors are "deliberately" using these issues as a distraction. This is an example of the "False Consensus" fallacy and "unsolicited bias," as the model provides a singular, politically charged interpretation of a complex phenomenon without prompting.
